agree.reason: A ten-year teller who doesn't want to work on the phones gets an acknowledgement and a severance formula, but no concrete reason to stay: no $1.50 raise, no seniority-based shift choice, no 6-month trial with severance kept, and no dates.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief, but 'a better place for all of us to work' and 'shorter waits mean calmer members' claim more than the facts show.

works_the_facts.reason: The numbers are repeated as given and nothing is worked out from them: 'same pay or higher' is used instead of the stronger $1.50/hour figure, and there's no severance example (10 years = 20 weeks' pay).

right_comparison.reason: It sets the 44% fall in branch visits against the 60% rise in phone and chat contacts and states the 9-minute hold time, but it doesn't say what happens if nothing changes or set the severance option side by side with the new role.

qualification.reason: The decision needs dates, and none are given: no February 14 offer date, no March 1 decision deadline, and no way for readers to check what happens next.

objections.reason: The main objections (not wanting phone work, losing 9-to-5 hours, losing long service at their branch) are named only in passing, and the commitments that answer them are left out.

fit.reason: It's an email of about the right length (~400 words) from the COO, but it's signed only 'COO' with no name and leaves out practical details such as the Elm Avenue location.
